In short: there are positive correlations between violent media and violent thoughts/behavior. Correlation does not imply causation, i.e. it could be that more agressive people cause people to enjoy more agressive movies/games.

Unfortunately science and opinion are related, more so in social sciences than hard sciences. If a researcher believes violent games cause violent behavior, the chance of 'finding' this relationship increases. Double-blind controlled experiments would be a bit difficult.

It's also worth noting what exactly qualifies as "increased aggression" to social sciences. This isn't stuff like measuring who gets into more fistfights, it's stuff like "Complete the following word: explo_e", and if you complete it with a D instead of an R, you're "more aggressive". So the headline will be "Study finds link between playing video games and violence", and everyone thinks they proved that video games make people significantly more likely to get into fights or shoot people, but what they actually found out is that a small percentage of people will fill in slightly different crossword answers. And who even knows how many similar studies were conducted which came up with no results or a negative correlation and were ditched because it didn't confirm what the researchers wanted to say.
